startup.name: Complir
startup.description: AI-powered product compliance platform that makes it easy for retailers to launch and scale products across borders without drowning in regulatory work. Complir's AI agents handle the regulations and documentation across every market you sell in - and keep your entire catalogue audit-ready.

yc_acceptance.basis: Roughly 1 percent base rate. Conditional on acceptance this is a note: a thirteen person Copenhagen team with a clear Vanta comparison and a regulatory driver, so the estimate sits above the base.
yc_acceptance.why_it_fails: YC would most plausibly worry about a European team selling to retailers with long sales cycles and regulation that varies by country, and whether AI agents can be trusted for compliance. The estimate leans on the cohort base rates in stage_benchmarks.md, where later rounds are rare and slow, and on what happened to comparable YC companies such as upcodes and pluralith.

ladder.why_it_fails: The seed most plausibly fails if investors see consulting work rather than software, because every market has its own rules and documents. UpCodes, a YC building code platform, grew slowly and Pluralith, a compliance documentation tool, did not show a later round. Without paid retailers by demo day the Vanta comparison alone will not close a round.

killers.evidence: Each country has different rules and documents, which look like services. This is visible in the comparable YC companies and the competitor sources listed in this evaluation.
killers.mitigation: Focus on EU GPSR and a few categories first.

technical_complexity.rationale: Agents that read regulations and generate technical documents are feasible, but accuracy and audit readiness across many markets are hard. A small team can cover one regulation set first.

takeover_risk.rationale: Incumbents have distribution but not the regulatory depth. The timeline is an estimate for a well resourced rival with existing distribution and an incentive to copy the idea.

evidence.claim: The EU General Product Safety Regulation applied from December 2024 to any seller into the EU, creating documentation duties.
Law firm analysis shows the scope covers non food consumer products and some B2B goods.

actions: Sign five pilot retailers in the EU.

pros.evidence: GPSR applies to all sellers into the EU.

pros.point: A clear analogy to a proven category.

brand.rationale: The name is invented but echoes compliance and is easy to say. It resembles many recent invented B2B names and will not change outcomes much.

narrative.headline: A timely compliance idea with a good analogy, held back by local regulatory work and a long retail sales cycle.
narrative.general_summary: Complir sells AI product compliance to retailers. A new EU regulation gives it a clear trigger and a thirteen person team is large for a spring 2026 company. The likeliest path is a seed, then a harder Series A as investors test whether it scales like software. UpCodes and Pluralith show slower paths. Data on recent B2B Series B outcomes is thin. The step odds are anchored on the 2022 to 2025 B2B cohorts and the older 2018 to 2021 cohort, which differ a lot, so treat the later rounds as wide ranges.

assumptions: Founders and customers were not provided.
